subtitle: Slow-steamed beef cheeks
verso: A Sunday without barbacoa is a Sunday without joy.
story: In Hidalgo, barbacoa is lamb wrapped in maguey leaves and cooked overnight in a pit, with a pot underneath catching the juices for consomé. This home version steams beef with avocado leaves. Barbacoa is the Sunday late breakfast: in the north, families buy cachete (cheek), lengua (tongue) and cabeza (head) by the kilo on Sunday mornings.

ingredients.title: The meat
items: 3 lb beef cheeks (cachete), or chuck roast in large pieces
6 dried avocado leaves, toasted (or 1 tsp anise seed)

ingredients.title: Consomé
items: Chopped onion, cilantro, lime and salsa

steps: Rub the meat with the salt, pepper, cumin and garlic. Let stand 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge.
Put a rack or steamer basket in a tall pot with 4 cups water, the onion and the bay leaves underneath.
Lay banana leaves on the rack if you have them, add the avocado leaves and the meat, and fold the banana leaves over.
Cover tightly and steam on low 4–5 hours, adding hot water when needed, until the meat shreds easily.
Shred the meat. For the consomé, strain the liquid from under the rack, add the chickpeas, rice and carrot, and simmer 20 minutes.
Serve the barbacoa in tortillas with salsa, and the consomé in a cup on the side with chopped onion, cilantro and lime.

pressureCooker.time: 65 min high pressure + 20 min natural release
steps: Season the meat. Put the onion, bay leaves, avocado leaves and 1½ cups water in the pot and add the meat.
Shred the meat with a little of the liquid.
Strain the remaining liquid, add the chickpeas, rice and carrot, and cook on Sauté 15 minutes for consomé.

tips: Mexican avocado leaves taste of anise. Toast them a few seconds on the comal before using.
Cheeks are full of collagen. Don't trim them too lean or you'll lose the silky texture.

variations.name: Salsa Borracha
variations.subtitle: Pasilla salsa with beer or pulque
variations.note: The classic partner for barbacoa, traditionally made with pulque.

items: ½ cup pulque or light Mexican beer
Crumbled queso añejo and chopped onion, to finish

steps: Toast the pasillas briefly and soak 10 minutes.
Grind in the molcajete or blend with the garlic, onion, beer and salt. Keep it a little coarse.
Top with queso añejo and chopped onion.
